tests.title: Unit 2: Introduction to English Composition – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: A paragraph is:
options: A group of related sentences developing one main idea, usually 5–8 sentences long
questions.explanation: It usually has a topic sentence, supporting sentences and a concluding sentence.

questions.question_text: The three parts of a paragraph are:
options: Topic sentence, supporting sentences and concluding sentence

questions.question_text: A topic sentence is:
options: The sentence that states the main idea of the paragraph, usually placed first
questions.explanation: It controls the content of the paragraph.

questions.question_text: Which is the best topic sentence for a paragraph on "Importance of punctuality"?
options: Punctuality is a habit that builds trust and success in both studies and work.
questions.explanation: It states a clear, focused main idea.

questions.question_text: Supporting sentences:
options: Develop the topic sentence with facts, examples and explanations
questions.explanation: They provide evidence for the main idea.

questions.question_text: A concluding sentence:
options: Summarises or restates the main idea and gives closure
questions.explanation: It should not add new points.

questions.question_text: Unity in a paragraph means:
options: Every sentence relates to the single main idea

questions.question_text: Coherence in a paragraph means:
options: Sentences are logically connected and flow smoothly
questions.explanation: It is achieved through order and transitions.

questions.question_text: Coherence can be achieved by:
options: Logical order, transitions and repeating key words or pronouns
questions.explanation: Consistent point of view also helps.

questions.question_text: Transitions such as "however", "for example", "therefore" and "first" show, respectively:
Methods of developing a paragraph include:
options: Examples, comparison, cause and effect, process and definition
questions.explanation: The choice depends on the purpose.

questions.question_text: The first step in writing a paragraph is to:
options: Choose and narrow the topic, then plan the main idea

questions.question_text: The topic sentence in "Exercise is vital. It improves heart health, builds strength and boosts mood." is:
Remove the irrelevant sentence: "Tea is popular in India. It is grown in Assam. Mountains are very tall. Many people drink it daily."
questions.explanation: It breaks the unity of the paragraph.

questions.question_text: The most coherent order is: (a) First, mix the flour and water. (b) Making dough is simple. (c) Finally, rest it for an hour. (d) Next, knead it for ten minutes.
questions.explanation: Topic sentence first, then steps in order.

questions.question_text: A suitable concluding sentence for "Reading builds vocabulary, improves concentration and reduces stress." is:
options: In short, reading is a simple habit with many benefits.

questions.question_text: A descriptive paragraph:
options: Paints a picture of a person, place or object using vivid details

questions.question_text: Descriptive paragraphs commonly follow:
options: Spatial order (e.g., top to bottom, left to right)

questions.question_text: Sensory details in description:
options: Appeal to sight, sound, smell, taste and touch to make the scene vivid
questions.explanation: They help the reader experience the scene.

questions.question_text: The best opening for a descriptive paragraph on "A busy railway station" is:
options: I went to the station yesterday and bought a ticket.
You should always buy a ticket.
The platform buzzed with the clatter of trolleys, shouting vendors and the steady hiss of arriving trains.
Railway stations are used to travel.
questions.explanation: It uses sound and visual details.

questions.question_text: The best opening for a descriptive paragraph on "Your college campus" is:
options: Tall neem trees line the red-brick paths that wind between the library and the sunlit courtyard.

questions.question_text: The best opening for a descriptive paragraph on "A rainy day" is:
options: Grey clouds sagged over the city as fat raindrops drummed on the tin roofs and the air smelt of wet earth.
questions.explanation: It appeals to sight, sound and smell.

questions.question_text: The best opening for a descriptive paragraph on "A marketplace during a festival" is:
options: The lanes glittered with strings of lights, and the air was thick with the smell of sweets, flowers and incense.

questions.question_text: The best opening for a descriptive paragraph on "Your favourite place in your city" is:
options: The lakeside promenade glows golden at sunset, with cool breeze and the soft murmur of strolling families.

questions.question_text: A narrative paragraph:
options: Tells a story or recounts an event in sequence
questions.explanation: It has characters, setting and plot.

tests.title: Unit 2: Introduction to English Composition – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: The order used in a narrative paragraph is:
questions.explanation: Events are narrated as they occurred.

questions.question_text: The tense mostly used in narration is:
questions.explanation: Present tense may be used for effect.

questions.question_text: The best opening for a narrative paragraph on "Your first day at college" is:
options: On my first day at college, I walked through the gates nervous and clutching my timetable.
questions.explanation: It starts the story in sequence.

questions.question_text: The best opening for a narrative paragraph on "A memorable journey" is:
options: Last summer, my family boarded the night train to Darjeeling, unaware how memorable the trip would be.

questions.question_text: The best opening for a narrative paragraph on "A time you solved a problem" is:
options: During my internship, the billing software crashed on the last day of the month, and I had to find a fix before evening.
questions.explanation: It names the event and context.

questions.question_text: The best opening for a narrative paragraph on "A lesson learnt from failure" is:
options: When I failed my first accounting test, I felt crushed, but that moment taught me how to study.
questions.explanation: It starts the story and hints at the lesson.

questions.question_text: The best opening for a narrative paragraph on "A day when everything went wrong" is:
options: My alarm did not ring, and from that moment the day unravelled one mishap after another.
questions.explanation: It begins the chain of events.

questions.question_text: An expository paragraph:
options: Explains or informs about a topic using facts and examples

questions.question_text: Characteristics of expository writing include:
options: Clear, factual, logical and objective language
questions.explanation: It uses facts, definitions and examples.

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for an expository paragraph on "How UPI works" is:
options: UPI lets users transfer money instantly between bank accounts using a virtual payment address and a PIN.
UPI is the best thing ever.

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for an expository paragraph on "Causes of inflation" is:
options: Inflation is caused mainly by rising demand, higher production costs and an increase in money supply.

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for an expository paragraph on "The importance of financial literacy" is:
options: I opened a bank account last year.
Financial literacy helps people manage money, avoid debt and plan for the future.

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for an expository paragraph on "How to prepare for an interview" is:
options: Preparing for an interview involves researching the company, practising answers and planning your attire.

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for an expository paragraph on "The benefits of sleep" is:
options: Adequate sleep improves memory, mood and physical health.

questions.question_text: A persuasive paragraph:
options: Tries to convince the reader to accept a viewpoint or take action

questions.question_text: Elements of a persuasive paragraph include:
options: A clear position, reasons, evidence and a call to action

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for a persuasive paragraph on "Why students should learn financial skills" is:
options: Students should learn financial skills because they prepare them to manage money wisely in adult life.
questions.explanation: It states a position with a reason.

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for a persuasive paragraph on "Why plastic bags should be banned" is:
options: Plastic bags should be banned because they pollute the environment and harm wildlife.

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for a persuasive paragraph on "Why companies should allow remote work" is:
options: Companies should allow remote work because it raises productivity and widens the talent pool.

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for a persuasive paragraph on "Why public transport should be preferred" is:
options: Public transport should be preferred because it reduces traffic, pollution and travel costs.

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for a persuasive paragraph on "Why every student should do an internship" is:
options: Every student should do an internship because it gives practical experience that classrooms cannot offer.
questions.explanation: It states a claim with a reason.

questions.question_text: The correct match is:
options: Descriptive – picture; narrative – story; expository – explain; persuasive – convince

questions.question_text: "The old banyan tree towered over the courtyard, its roots sprawling like giant fingers" is:
"First, I opened the app. Then I entered the amount. Finally, I confirmed the payment." is:
"You must vote. Your vote shapes the future." is:
questions.explanation: It tries to convince the reader to act.

tests.title: Unit 2: Introduction to English Composition – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: "Last Sunday, my brother and I went trekking. We started early, reached the summit at noon and came back exhausted but happy." is:
An essay is:
options: A structured piece of writing on a topic with an introduction, body and conclusion

questions.question_text: The parts of an essay are:
The function of an introduction is to:
options: Hook the reader, give background and state the thesis

questions.question_text: Common ways to begin an essay (hooks) include:
options: A question, a quotation, a statistic or a short anecdote

questions.question_text: A thesis statement is:
options: A sentence that states the central argument or main idea of the whole essay
questions.explanation: It is usually at the end of the introduction.

questions.question_text: The best thesis statement for an essay on "Social media and business" is:
options: This essay is about social media.
Social media transforms business by improving marketing reach, customer engagement and brand building.
questions.explanation: It states a clear, arguable point.

questions.question_text: A thesis statement differs from a topic sentence in that a thesis statement:
options: Covers the main idea of the whole essay, while a topic sentence covers one paragraph
questions.explanation: Each topic sentence supports the thesis.

questions.question_text: The function of body paragraphs is to:
options: Develop and support the thesis with evidence, one main idea per paragraph
questions.explanation: They contain topic sentences and support.

questions.question_text: A conclusion should restate the thesis and summarise the main points, while avoiding:
questions.explanation: New points belong in the body.

questions.question_text: Types of essays include:
An argumentative essay differs from a persuasive essay in that an argumentative essay:
options: Relies mainly on logic and evidence, while a persuasive essay also uses emotional appeal

questions.question_text: The writing process consists of:
options: Pre-writing, drafting, revising, editing and proofreading

questions.question_text: Pre-writing techniques include:
options: Brainstorming, free writing and mind mapping

questions.question_text: A mind map is:
options: A diagram showing ideas branching from a central topic

questions.question_text: An outline is:
options: A structured plan listing the main points and sub-points of an essay

questions.question_text: Revising differs from editing in that revising:
options: Improves content, organisation and ideas, while editing corrects grammar, spelling and style

questions.question_text: Proofreading is:
options: The final check for spelling, punctuation and typing errors

questions.question_text: Plagiarism is:
options: Using someone else's words or ideas without giving credit; it is avoided by citing sources and paraphrasing

questions.question_text: The best thesis for a 200-word essay on "Digital India" is:
options: Digital India is transforming governance, payments and education by expanding access to technology.
questions.explanation: It states a clear central idea.

questions.question_text: The best thesis for an essay on "Importance of ethics in business" is:
options: Ethical practices build trust, protect reputation and ensure long-term business success.

questions.question_text: The best thesis for an essay on "Role of women in the economy" is:
options: Women contribute to the economy as workers, entrepreneurs and consumers, and their participation drives growth.

questions.question_text: The best thesis for an essay on "Climate change and business" is:
options: Climate change poses risks and opportunities for businesses, requiring sustainable practices.

questions.question_text: The best thesis for an essay on "Artificial intelligence: boon or bane?" is:
options: Artificial intelligence is more of a boon than a bane when used responsibly.
questions.explanation: It takes a position on the question.

questions.question_text: The best thesis for an essay on "Start-ups and youth entrepreneurship" is:
options: Start-ups give young people opportunities to innovate, create jobs and boost the economy.

tests.title: Unit 2: Introduction to English Composition – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: The best opening for an essay on "A visit to a bank" is:
options: Last Monday, I visited my local bank for the first time to open a savings account.

questions.question_text: The best thesis for an essay on "My career goals" is:
options: My goal is to become a chartered accountant, and I am preparing through study and internships.
questions.explanation: It states a clear personal goal.

questions.question_text: The best thesis for an essay on "Cashless economy" is:
options: A cashless economy increases transparency, convenience and efficiency but needs safe digital infrastructure.

questions.question_text: An outline for "Work-life balance" would most logically include:
An outline for "Pros and cons of online education" would most logically include:
A good introduction for "Importance of financial planning" includes:
options: A hook, background and a thesis statement
questions.explanation: E.g., a statistic, context and the central claim.

questions.question_text: A good conclusion for "Social media and business" would:
options: Restate the thesis, summarise the main points and end with a closing thought
Repeat the introduction word for word

questions.question_text: The stronger version of the weak thesis "This essay is about pollution" is:
options: This essay will talk about pollution.
Pollution harms health and the economy, and stricter regulation is needed to control it.
questions.explanation: It takes a clear, arguable position.

questions.question_text: A style tip for formal essay writing is to:
options: Use formal vocabulary, clear structure and an objective tone

questions.question_text: Contractions and slang should be avoided in formal essays because:
options: They sound informal and reduce credibility
They are unclear in all cases
questions.explanation: Formal writing needs a professional tone.

questions.question_text: A consistent tone in an essay is maintained by:
options: Choosing a style and vocabulary appropriate to the audience and keeping it throughout

questions.question_text: An essay differs from a report in that an essay:
options: Develops an argument in continuous prose, while a report presents organised findings with headings

questions.question_text: An essay is made coherent by:
options: Logical order, transitions and linking each paragraph to the thesis
questions.explanation: Each paragraph should flow into the next.

questions.question_text: Revision is important because it:
options: Improves clarity, organisation and quality of the draft

questions.question_text: A common essay error is:
options: Weak thesis, poor organisation and grammar mistakes

questions.question_text: Useful phrases for an introduction, body and conclusion respectively are:
An effective hook is:
options: A surprising fact, question or quotation that grabs attention, e.g., "Did you know India makes over 100 crore UPI transactions a day?"

questions.question_text: In body paragraphs, evidence is used by:
options: Supporting each claim with facts, statistics, examples or expert opinion

questions.question_text: Counter-arguments in a persuasive essay are addressed by:
options: Acknowledging the opposing view and refuting it with evidence

questions.question_text: A call to action is:
options: A closing statement urging readers to do something, e.g., "Start saving today."
questions.explanation: It is common in persuasive writing.

questions.question_text: Word choice is improved by:
options: Using precise, specific and appropriate words instead of vague ones

questions.question_text: A paragraph comparing online shopping and in-store shopping would use the pattern:
options: Point-by-point or block comparison with words like "whereas" and "similarly"

questions.question_text: A good opening for a paragraph defining "entrepreneur" is:
options: An entrepreneur is a person who starts and manages a business, taking financial risks in the hope of profit.
questions.explanation: A definition names the term, class and distinguishing features.

questions.question_text: The best topic sentence for a cause-and-effect paragraph on "Why people miss deadlines" is:
options: People miss deadlines mainly because of poor planning, procrastination and unrealistic time estimates.
questions.explanation: It names the effect and causes.

questions.question_text: Notes: "benefits of teamwork — shared workload, diverse ideas, faster solutions, better morale." The best paragraph is:
options: Teamwork offers many benefits: it shares the workload, brings diverse ideas, speeds up solutions and improves morale.
Teamwork is hard and I dislike it.
questions.explanation: It turns the points into connected sentences.
